evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Own data quality, validation, testing, monitoring, and governance across the analytics stack.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities are dominated by quality, validation, testing, monitoring, governance, CI, and 'quality first mindset' language with no velocity/shipping-speed phrasing, so this is rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: Every product decision, customer insight, experiment, and business metric depends on reliable, well modelled data.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Errors affect product decisions, experimentation, and business metrics at a B2B SaaS company, but no financial-reporting, regulatory, or audit language is used, so this is moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity: Own the performance, reliability, and continuous improvement of Doodle's analytics platform.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: An analytics platform, semantic layer, and dbt-based transformation pipelines already exist and are being owned/improved rather than built from scratch, with governance and CI practices in place, indicating mid maturity.
evidence.jd_authorship: Design, build, and maintain scalable analytics data models using dbt and modern data engineering practices.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Bullets name specific tools (dbt, Airflow, Redshift, Athena, Spark, pandas) with precise application context across platform, modelling, quality, and experimentation domains, giving a clear picture of day-to-day work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Working closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Finance, and Leadership
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Responsibilities span product analytics/experimentation and cross-functional collaboration with Marketing, Finance, and Leadership with no single dominant audience, so this is mixed.
evidence.autonomy_level: you will own the analytics platform that enables self service insights across Doodle
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Strategic ownership verbs dominate ('own', 'define, document, and maintain trusted business metrics', 'advise teams on analytics architecture'), indicating direction-setting rather than scoped execution.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No AI tooling or AI-related responsibility is mentioned anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing: Own data quality, validation, testing, monitoring, and governance across the analytics stack.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and data quality are explicitly framed as something the candidate owns, using the ownership verb 'Own', so this is responsibility.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Own data quality, validation, testing, monitoring, and governance across the analytics stack.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Quality, reliability, trust, and governance language recurs throughout ('trusted data foundation', 'Establish standards that improve data reliability, consistency, security, and trust'), anchoring a high loss-aversion register.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Own the performance, reliability, and continuous improvement of Doodle's analytics platform.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role improves, evolves, and continuously improves an existing analytics platform and semantic layer rather than building from zero, so this is fix_scale.
evidence.loss_aversion: Establish standards that improve data reliability, consistency, security, and trust.

responsibilities: As an Analytics Engineer, you will own the analytics platform that enables self service insights across Doodle.
Design, build, and maintain scalable analytics data models using dbt and modern data engineering practices.
Develop reliable transformation pipelines that convert raw product data into trusted, business ready datasets.
Own the performance, reliability, and continuous improvement of Doodle's analytics platform.
Define, document, and maintain trusted business metrics used across the company.
Build and evolve a scalable semantic layer that enables consistent reporting and self service analytics.
Ensure data definitions remain accurate, accessible, and aligned across teams.
Own data quality, validation, testing, monitoring, and governance across the analytics stack.
Implement best practices for documentation, version control, CI, and automated testing.
Establish standards that improve data reliability, consistency, security, and trust.
Partner with Product Managers and Analysts to enable experimentation, funnel analysis, retention analysis, and customer insights.
Support product launches by providing reliable measurement frameworks and trusted analytics.
Enable accurate A B testing through high quality event modelling and instrumentation.
Work closely with Product, Engineering, Data, Marketing, Finance, and Leadership teams.
Translate business questions into scalable data models, trusted metrics, and actionable insights.
Advise teams on analytics architecture, data modelling standards, and best practices.
Influence product and business decisions by making data reliable, accessible, and easy to use.
